story: FIRST-MOVER WINDOW and the best Kaspa redirect in this batch: Blast, the Paradigm-backed Ethereum layer 2 that was once a $2B+ network, is winding down because costs outpace revenue, after its assets plunged 98%. Named backer, hard numbers, and ZERO coverage across the 10 watchlist creators (by title). Primary sources: Blast's own wind-down announcement plus the TVL history on L2Beat / DefiLlama. story: Hack week, and the contested part is who gets to say no. NEAR Intents was drained for $3.8M, named the attacker, issued a 48-hour ultimatum and recovered all of it (Decrypt even asked 'was it a bullish hack?'). Days earlier NEAR had rejected $50M in swaps from the North Korea-linked Bitget hacker, who then moved to a Zcash privacy pool, and Chainalysis used AI to trace the $387M Bitget hack to North Korea, which set off a THORChain vs NEAR neutrality fight. Separately, a Zano exploiter minted more than a quadrillion fUSD before the chain was ROLLED BACK. Polymarket prices total 2026 hacks above $3B at 62%. PEER CHECK (by title): Fire Hustle has a NEAR video but it reads as price talk, not the hack. Redirect: an intents layer that can veto swaps and a chain that can rewind both have an operator; a proof-of-work chain has hashpower, not an undo button.
titles: They Found The Hacker In 48 HOURS (And Got Every Dollar Back)
